title: Galactic Atlas
scope: GKI-03 initial Atlas: Jameson Memorial and Shinrarta Dezhra, Jameson's Crash Site in HIP 12099, three rediscovered INRA bases, the Generation Ship Lycaon and Hutton Orbital, with the people, organisations, events and discoveries that connect them, and the crash site's encoded-material scanning.
game_version: Lore records are not tied to a game version. The crash site's nine data points and position reflect the 2025 site update as reported on 2026-10-29. Identifiers were read from EDSM on 2026-10-29.
rights_basis: Original OmniCOVAS records of Elite Dangerous game facts and lore: names, dates, identifiers, coordinates, relationships and short factual summaries written in OmniCOVAS's own words. No wiki prose, quotations, images or tables are reproduced; sources are credited per claim.

distribution.basis: GKI-03 content audit (2026-10-29): every record is an original OmniCOVAS statement of game facts or lore, checked with the curator expression check against the cited wiki revisions and the community guide.

entities.name: Shinrarta Dezhra
entities.summary: Permit-locked home system of the Pilots Federation, entered only with the Founders World permit.

attributes.significance: Headquarters of the Pilots Federation and home of Jameson Memorial, the station most veteran commanders aim to reach.

claims.text: Entry needs the Founders World permit. The usual route is an Elite rank in any of the five ranked careers; Kickstarter backers held it from the start.
The system is the seat of the Pilots Federation, and Elite pilots may retire here.
A tie-in novel explains the name as a shortened blend of Russian and Arabic words for life, she saw and hope.
Powerplay cannot take control of this system or exploit it.
The Dark Wheel keeps a presence here, and the Engineer Lori Jameson works from Jameson Base on Shinrarta Dezhra A 1.

entities.name: Founders World
entities.summary: Terraformed Earth-like world in Shinrarta Dezhra holding the Pilots Federation headquarters.

attributes.significance: The world that gives the system permit its name and the place where Elite pilots are said to retire.

claims.text: A terraformed Earth-like world with a breathable atmosphere and native life, orbiting the star Shinrarta Dezhra.
The Founders World permit is named after this planet, itself a nod to the game's Kickstarter founders.

entities.name: HIP 12099
entities.summary: Remote system holding the wreck of John Jameson's Cobra and the abandoned INRA base Stack.

attributes.significance: Where the story of John Jameson's last flight ends, and a well-known encoded-material stop.

claims.text: John Jameson's sabotaged Cobra came down on the moon HIP 12099 1 B.
INRA also ran a base called Stack on the neighbouring moon 1 A, where captured Thargoid specimens were studied.

entities.name: HIP 12099 1 b
entities.summary: Landable moon of HIP 12099 where Jameson's Cobra crashed.

attributes.significance: The body a commander must land on to visit Jameson's Crash Site.

location.note: The wiki writes the moon as 1 B; the game names it with a lower-case letter.

claims.text: The second moon of the first planet in HIP 12099, and landable.

entities.name: Jameson's Crash Site
entities.summary: Surface site on HIP 12099 1 b where the wreck of John Jameson's Cobra Mk III lies among data points.

attributes.significance: The resting place of a legendary pilot betrayed by INRA, and one of the best-known places to gather high-grade encoded materials.
attributes.period: Crash during the First Thargoid War; found 25 November 3303

location.note: Position as given for the current game after the 2025 site update. The wiki's earlier figure, -54.3, -50.3, agrees to one decimal place.

claims.text: The wreck is John Jameson's own Cobra Mk III, registration JJ-386, which INRA sent on a collision course with this moon.
The crash site was located on 25 November 3303, roughly 150 years after Jameson disappeared.
No body can be seen through the canopy and nobody knows who placed the beacons around the wreck, so whether Jameson survived the impact remains open.
Nine data points surround the wreck since a 2025 update (four before). Scanning them gives encoded materials of grades 2 to 5.
After the first visit the site stays listed in the ship's navigation panel, so the coordinates are only needed once.
The site is abandoned and has no defences; an SRV is enough and no weapons, shields or cargo space are needed.

entities.name: Stack
entities.summary: Abandoned INRA research base on HIP 12099 1 a where living Thargoid specimens were studied.

attributes.significance: Shows how far INRA's experiments went, in the same system where Jameson's Cobra fell.
attributes.period: First Thargoid War era; found 24 November 3303

location.note: The wiki lists the moon as 1 A; EDSM gives the game's body name 1 a with BodyID 15.

claims.text: INRA built a secure octagonal pit here to hold and test a captured Thargoid, which records show tried to escape several times.
Rediscovered by commanders on 24 November 3303 during the search for INRA's bases.

entities.name: Taylor Keep
entities.summary: Abandoned INRA base in 12 Trianguli where Jameson's Cobra was armed for his final mission.

attributes.significance: The last place John Jameson stopped before the mission that ended the First Thargoid War and his life.

location.note: The wiki names the body 1 A, but the game's body list for 12 Trianguli has no body of that name (the nearest is 12 Trianguli A 1). Until that is resolved the base is matched to the system only.

claims.text: INRA loaded mycoid-armed missiles from Klatt Enterprises onto Jameson's own Cobra here, after modifying the ship for the mission.
Rediscovered on 25 November 3303, the same day Jameson's wreck was found.
The documented body name does not match the game's naming for this system, so OmniCOVAS does not claim an exact landing position.

entities.name: Hollis Gateway
entities.summary: Derelict INRA research site where work on Thargoid technology first revealed the mycoid effect.

attributes.significance: Where the weapon that won the First Thargoid War was first noticed, and the first INRA base to be found again.

claims.text: A junior researcher studying farming uses of Thargoid technology noticed that a fungus damaged it, and took the finding over the head of a dismissive superior.
Corroded tanks on the base carry mycohazard warnings and have leaked what may be the weapon itself.
Its rediscovery on 9 October 3303 began the hunt for INRA's other bases.

entities.name: Generation Ship Lycaon
entities.summary: Derelict generation ship drifting in the Alaunus system, the first of the lost generation ships to be found.

attributes.significance: Opened the search for humanity's lost colony ships; its logs tell how an alien illness ended the voyage.

location.note: Recorded when found as about 22,000 ls from the 10th planet towards Horae. Generation ships drift, so locate its present signal with the FSS.

claims.text: Found on 23 April 3303, ahead of every other lost generation ship.
Its logs describe a flu-like microorganism, picked up while surveying an asteroid and untouched by any vaccine, that killed everyone aboard before the ship lost power.
The Full Spectrum System Scanner identifies a generation ship's signal from anywhere in its system; listening posts give clues to where to look.
Generation ships were sub-light colony arks launched from 2097 onwards, made obsolete once hyperdrives arrived; a small share never reached their destinations.

entities.name: Alpha Centauri
entities.summary: Neighbouring star system to Sol, with Hutton Orbital orbiting far out near Proxima Centauri.

attributes.significance: Home of Hutton Orbital, one of the best-known pilgrimages in human space.

claims.text: Hutton Orbital orbits Eden, a world circling Proxima Centauri, far from the system's arrival star.

entities.name: Hutton Orbital
entities.summary: Outpost in Alpha Centauri famous for lying about 0.22 light years from the system's arrival point.

attributes.significance: A rite of passage for new pilots and the origin of the Hutton Mug, a rare good created through a community vote.

claims.text: It lies about 6.78 million light seconds from the arrival star, roughly an hour and a half of supercruise at full throttle; the SCO frame shift drive shortens the trip at a higher fuel cost.
Documented rare goods: the Hutton Mug and Centauri Mega Gin.
Players chose the Hutton Mug in a vote on a new rare good; production began after a community goal delivered scrap here, despite a blockade by other players.
A long-running joke promises a free Anaconda on arrival. The station has no shipyard or large pads, so the offer is not real.
An outpost without large landing pads or a shipyard, as documented at review.

entities.name: Cobra Mk III JJ-386
entities.summary: John Jameson's personal Cobra Mk III, now a wreck at Jameson's Crash Site.

attributes.significance: The ship that carried mycoid to the Thargoids, and the source of Jameson's last recorded words.

claims.text: Built long before today's Cobra Mk III: its canopy is smaller, it has one forward hardpoint hatch and its thrusters are laid out differently. Older than the frame shift drive, it most likely flew with an earlier hyperspace drive.
Scanning the wreck itself plays Jameson's final logs, recorded for his son.
INRA modified the ship for the mission, including a program that shut its systems down once the missiles were away.

entities.name: John Jameson
entities.summary: Celebrated independent pilot of the 3100s who delivered INRA's mycoid weapon and never came home.

attributes.significance: His mission ended the First Thargoid War, and the truth about it, found in 3303, turned INRA from a heroic memory into a scandal.
attributes.period: 3100s; lost during the First Thargoid War

claims.text: Renowned for both exploration and combat, he became a model for generations of pilots.
INRA hired him to deliver the mycoid weapon, telling him it would only disable Thargoid hyperdrives.
He got through a Thargoid hive ship's defences, fired the missiles and got away, only for his scans to show the weapon killing those aboard.
INRA's hidden program then shut his ship down on a course into HIP 12099 1 B, so he could not report what the weapon did. He recorded a last log for his son.
Whether he died on impact or survived for a while is not known.
Jameson Memorial is named for a Jameson, but no source says it is John. OmniCOVAS does not link him to the station as its namesake.

entities.name: Peter Jameson
entities.summary: The earliest known Jameson and the first pilot awarded the Pilots Federation's Elite rank.

attributes.significance: Began the Jameson family's place in Pilots Federation history around 3100.

claims.text: Received the Elite rank around 3100, the first pilot to do so, and carried the badge on his Cobra Mk III.
A fragment of his Cobra from a fight with pirates in Reshas is kept in a local museum there.
He is John Jameson's ancestor. One wiki page calls him John's likely father, but the only source for that, an older game manual, is not treated as canon.

entities.name: Lori Jameson
entities.summary: John Jameson's great-granddaughter, an Engineer working from Jameson Base in Shinrarta Dezhra.

attributes.significance: No other living Jameson is known.

claims.text: Great-granddaughter of John Jameson and the only known living Jameson.
Her engineering workshop is Jameson Base in Shinrarta Dezhra; its details live in the Engineering workspace.

entities.name: Riri McAllister
entities.summary: Founder and coordinator of the League of Reparation, known by the codename Nexus.

attributes.significance: Built the League to avenge John Jameson, believing herself his descendant.

claims.text: Founded the League of Reparation and directed it as Nexus until her arrest in July 3304.
She claimed John Jameson as an ancestor. Investigators could not check the claim because her records list her as an orphan with no known parents.

entities.name: CMDR Robbie Junior
entities.summary: Commander credited with finding Jameson's crashed Cobra in 3303.

attributes.significance: Credited by the wiki with locating the crash site.

claims.text: Named by the wiki as the commander who located the crash site on 25 November 3303.

entities.name: Intergalactic Naval Reserve Arm
entities.summary: Covert joint Federal and Imperial organisation that fought the Thargoids and created the mycoid weapon.

attributes.significance: Ended the First Thargoid War by means its leaders hid, including the deliberate loss of John Jameson.

claims.text: Set up jointly by the Federation and the Empire to counter Thargoid incursions; it became public in 3193 and disbanded in 3253 after losing public and political support.
Older lore gives different founding dates and even a different name, so the founding year is not settled.
Its research turned a fungus that damaged Thargoid technology into the mycoid weapon, tested it on captured Thargoids and mass-produced it.
From October 3303 commanders found a network of its abandoned bases, whose records revealed the programme and Jameson's fate.
In December 3303 the Emperor and the Alliance Prime Minister publicly condemned INRA's conduct, including how it used Jameson.

entities.name: Pilots Federation
entities.summary: Politically neutral organisation of independent pilots, founded in 2805, that issues every commander's licence and rank.

attributes.significance: The organisation every commander belongs to; it governs Shinrarta Dezhra.

claims.text: Formed in 2805, when private starship ownership boomed, to let pilots share trade-route information and protect each other from pirates.
Rates pilots in several careers; an Elite rank is the usual way to earn the Founders World permit.
Its headquarters is on Founders World in Shinrarta Dezhra.

entities.name: Jameson family
entities.summary: Family of famous pilots tied to the Pilots Federation, from Peter Jameson to the Engineer Lori Jameson.

attributes.significance: Two of its members rank among the most renowned pilots in human history, and Jameson Memorial honours one of them.

claims.text: Known members are Peter Jameson, John Jameson, John's unnamed son, Dan Jameson and Lori Jameson.
Jameson Memorial is named for a member of the family, but the sources do not say which one.

entities.name: League of Reparation
entities.summary: Terrorist group that killed descendants of INRA staff in the name of INRA's victims, dismantled in 3304.

attributes.significance: Showed how the INRA revelations, and Jameson's story above all, still drew blood 150 years later.

claims.text: Hunted the descendants of INRA personnel, leaving the words For Jameson at its killings.
A taskforce of the three superpowers declared it dismantled on 27 July 3304 after capturing or killing every member.

entities.name: First Thargoid War
entities.summary: Humanity's first war with the Thargoids, fought from 3125 to 3151 and largely forgotten afterwards.

attributes.significance: Ended with the Thargoids leaving human space after INRA's mycoid strike, and helped bring down the Galactic Cooperative.

claims.text: The Galactic Cooperative and INRA defended human space; INRA tracked the Thargoids and built the means to stop them.
The Thargoids withdrew from human space by 3151, which is credited to the mycoid weapon.
Captured Thargoid ships later let the Alliance develop the frame shift drive.

entities.name: Jameson's final mission
entities.summary: INRA's mycoid strike on a Thargoid hive ship, flown by John Jameson, which ended in his ship's sabotage and crash.

attributes.significance: The act credited with ending the First Thargoid War, and the betrayal its rediscovery exposed.
attributes.period: Late in the First Thargoid War

claims.text: Prepared at Taylor Keep, where INRA armed Jameson's Cobra with mycoid missiles.
The strike succeeded, the ship was shut down by INRA and fell on HIP 12099 1 B, where its final logs survived.

entities.name: Rediscovery of the INRA bases
entities.summary: The 3303 search in which commanders found abandoned INRA bases and the records of the mycoid programme.

attributes.significance: Brought the hidden history of the First Thargoid War back to light and led to Jameson's wreck.

claims.text: Began with Hollis Gateway on 9 October 3303; Stack followed on 24 November and Taylor Keep on 25 November.
Logs at the bases told the story of mycoid from discovery to deployment.

entities.name: Discovery of Jameson's crash site
entities.summary: The finding of John Jameson's Cobra on HIP 12099 1 B on 25 November 3303.

attributes.significance: Settled a century-and-a-half mystery and confirmed INRA's betrayal through Jameson's own logs.

claims.text: The wreck was located on 25 November 3303 at the coordinates now known as Jameson's Crash Site.
Its logs fed the public condemnation of INRA in December 3303.

entities.name: League of Reparation killings
entities.summary: The 3304 campaign of assassinations, signed For Jameson, and the taskforce that ended it.

attributes.significance: Linked Jameson's name to a terror campaign within a year of his wreck being found.

claims.text: Imperial Senator Nestor Cartesius was found murdered on 20 April 3304 beside a note reading For Jameson; the League was exposed two weeks later.
The INRA page dates the Senator's murder to 3303; the League and Jameson pages give 3304, which OmniCOVAS follows.

entities.name: Thargoid attack on Shinrarta Dezhra
entities.summary: Surprise Thargoid assault on the Pilots Federation's home system in September 3310, repelled by commanders.

attributes.significance: The only time the permit was lifted for every commander, who arrived in their hundreds to defend Jameson Memorial.

claims.text: The Thargoids struck the system on 19 September 3310; the assault was defeated by 23 September.
Jameson Memorial stayed largely operational, repairing and rearming defenders throughout.
The Pilots Federation suspended the permit requirement during the attack, then restored it.

entities.name: Discovery of the Generation Ship Lycaon
entities.summary: The first finding of a lost generation ship, in Alaunus on 23 April 3303.

attributes.significance: Started the search for the Missing that turned up sixteen generation ships.

claims.text: Found in Alaunus on 23 April 3303; the wiki credits CMDR Lexic Meise.
Sixteen lost generation ships have been confirmed since then.

entities.name: Scan the data points at Jameson's Crash Site
entities.summary: Land at the crash site and scan its data points from an SRV for encoded materials.

steps.text: Fly to HIP 12099 1 b. On a first visit map the moon with probes and head for -54.37, -50.35; later visits can pick the site from the navigation panel.
Land beside the wreck and deploy the SRV.
Scan each data point with the SRV's data link scanner until all nine are done; the last one is the wreck itself.

claims.text: Direct drops are Adaptive Encryptors Capture (grade 5), Atypical Encryption Archives (grade 4), Cracked Industrial Firmware (grade 3) and Modified Consumer Firmware (grade 2).
Community guides report resetting the points by returning to the main menu and reloading once the data store is full. This is a player technique, not a documented game feature.

Guides report that collecting Adaptive Encryptors Capture here and converting it at an encoded Material Trader fills other encoded types faster than gathering them directly. This is a community efficiency estimate.

extends.name: Jameson Memorial
extends.summary: Orbis starport in Shinrarta Dezhra, named for a member of the Jameson family, that sells every ship and almost every module.

attributes.significance: The Pilots Federation's showpiece starport, a goal for every commander chasing Elite, and a Guardian Technology Broker station.

location.note: Parent body not recorded: the wiki says the station orbits Founders World, while EDSM's current record names another body and a 3,286 ls arrival distance.

claims.text: An Orbis starport in Shinrarta Dezhra.
Named in honour of a member of the Jameson family; the sources do not say which one, so OmniCOVAS names no individual.
The wiki places the station in orbit of Founders World. EDSM's record, read on 2026-10-29, lists a different parent body and arrival distance. OmniCOVAS does not choose between them.

Documented as selling every ship and almost every module at a 10% discount. Not stocked: one-off human technology broker items, Enhanced Performance Thrusters and the smallest (class 1) Corrosion Resistant Cargo Rack. Live stock is not tracked here.
The only seller of the rare good Waters of Shintara.
Hosts a Guardian Technology Broker; Guardian modules unlocked there can be bought in its outfitting.

relationships.note: Named for a member of the Jameson family. Which member is not specified.

relationships.period: As documented on the reviewed wiki revision (2026-10-29). Live faction control is not tracked.
